b/openspec/changes/seed-scenario-suite-and-nightly-cross-vendor-parity-runs/design.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,538 @@\n+# Design: Seed scenario suite and nightly cross-vendor parity runs\n+\n+## Context\n+\n+ri-15 (`build-agent-trajectory-scenario-harness`) built the harness library in\n+`packages/agent-scenarios/`. Its learnings that constrain this design:\n+\n+- The **deterministic goal-gate scorer is authoritative**; the LLM judge is additive\n+  and skip-never-fail. Nothing in this change lets a judge verdict create a\n+  capability gap or change a pass/fail.\n+- `command` gates resolve `python` to `sys.executable`.\n+- Live multi-vendor runs happen on the **GX10** with real CLIs; in-container and CI\n+  tests use `FakeExecutor`.\n+- `run_scenario` already distinguishes `deterministic_status` `pass | fail | error`,\n+  where `error` means the executor (CLI missing, non-zero exit, fixture failure)\n+  failed — that is infrastructure, not skill quality.\n+\n+Data flow after this change:\n+\n+```\n+nightly config ──► nightly.run()\n+                     │ 1. off-switch / kill-file / run lock\n+                     │ 2. flush gap spool (previous offline run)\n+                     │ 3. load suite, apply vendor allowlist, plan pairs\n+                     │ 4. cap check (max_pairs, per-vendor) — refuse if over\n+                     │ 5. run pairs (CLIVendorExecutor, skills_root, env scrub,\n+                     │    wall-clock budget → remaining pairs skipped_budget)\n+                     ├──► results_store.append(records)        (JSONL, trend)\n+                     ├──► findings_emitter.emit_findings(...)  (review-findings JSON)\n+                     └──► gap_emitter.emit(fail verdicts)      (memory API | spool)\n+                                          │\n+                       /improve-harness ◄─┘ (POST /memory/query, source:scenario-parity)\n+```\n+\n+## Decisions\n+\n+### D1 — Package-local runner and stores (Approach 1)\n+\n+All new runtime code lives in `packages/agent-scenarios/` as library modules with\n+thin CLI subcommands. Rationale and rejected alternatives are in `proposal.md`\n+(Approaches Considered). The coordinator is only a *consumer-facing sink* for\n+capability gaps through an endpoint that already exists (`POST /memory/store`).\n+\n+### D2 — Results store: append-only JSONL behind a `ResultsStore` interface\n+\n+**Choice**: one JSONL file (default `$XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-scenarios/results.jsonl`,\n+override via config `results.path` or `--store`). Two record types, both carrying\n+`schema_version: 1` and `record_type`:\n+\n+- `result` — one per (run_id, scenario_id, vendor): `recorded_at`, `run_id`,\n+  `scenario_id`, `skill_under_test`, `skill_family`, `vendor`,\n+  `deterministic_status` (`pass | fail | error | skipped_budget`), `failed_gates`\n+  (ids), `trajectory_status`, `duration_seconds`, `repo_sha`, `skills_sha`, `error`.\n+- `run` — one per nightly invocation: `run_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at`,\n+  `status` (`completed | disabled | cap_exceeded | budget_exhausted | locked |\n+  config_error`), `planned_pairs`, `executed_pairs`, `config_digest`, `vendors`,\n+  `repo_sha`, `skills_sha`, `reason`.\n+\n+Every listed field is present on every record (nullable fields as explicit `null`);\n+the schema also rejects contradictory states (`fail` with no failed gate, `pass` /\n+`skipped_budget` with failed gates, `error` without an `error` message).\n+\n+**Field mapping from ri-15 types** (verified against `models.py`; ri-15's\n+`VendorRunVerdict` has neither a duration nor a flat trajectory status):\n+`failed_gates` = `[g.gate_id for g in verdict.failed_gates]` (gates whose status is\n+`fail` or `error`, in scenario declaration order); `trajectory_status` =\n+`verdict.trajectory.status`; `duration_seconds` is measured by the nightly runner with\n+a monotonic clock around each single-vendor `run_scenario` call; `error` =\n+`verdict.error`. `skipped_budget` records carry `failed_gates: []`,\n+`duration_seconds: null`.\n+\n+**Incremental append**: the nightly runner appends each `result` record as soon as\n+its pair is scored, and the `run` record last. A run killed mid-way (systemd\n+`TimeoutStartSec`, SIGKILL, host reboot) therefore keeps every completed pair's\n+result; `result` records whose `run_id` has no `run` record are reported by\n+`results query`/`trend` as belonging to an *interrupted* run and are otherwise\n+counted normally — unless the run still holds the nightly run lock (a non-blocking\n+`flock` probe of `<state>/nightly.lock`), in which case they are reported as\n+*in progress*, so a query during the nightly window does not mislabel the live run.\n+\n+**Why not SQLite**: SQLite would also work, but at ~12k records/year a full scan is\n+cheap; JSONL is append-only by construction (no in-place updates, no migrations),\n+diffable, greppable, trivially rotated/backed up, and readers can tolerate partial\n+last lines from a crash. **Why not a coordinator table**: no cross-host consumer\n+exists yet; a migration + API + throwaway-DB tests is disproportionate for a\n+single-writer dataset (gatekeeper guidance: simplest durable store). The\n+`ResultsStore` protocol (`append(records)`, `iter_records(filters)`) leaves room for a\n+coordinator-backed implementation later.\n+\n+**Write safety**: appends take an exclusive `fcntl.flock` on the store file and write\n+whole lines with a trailing newline in one `write` + `fsync`; readers skip a\n+trailing partial line and records with an unknown `schema_version` (warning, not\n+error).\n+\n+**Queries** (`agent-scenarios results ...`):\n+- `query --vendor V --skill S --family F --scenario ID --since ISO --until ISO\n+  [--status ...] [--format json|table]` — raw matching `result` records.\n+- `trend --group-by vendor,skill|vendor,family|scenario,vendor --bucket day|week\n+  [filters]` — pass rate, counts per bucket (errors and `skipped_budget` reported\n+  separately and excluded from the pass-rate denominator).\n+- `latest [filters]` — most recent result per (scenario, vendor); the signal a\n+  future dispatcher gate would read.\n+\n+### D3 — Capability-gap emission: `source:scenario-parity` via the memory API, spool fallback\n+\n+For every `VendorRunVerdict` with `deterministic_status == \"fail\"` the gap emitter\n+builds one entry:\n+\n+```\n+event_type: \"capability_gap\"\n+summary:    \"[<vendor>] scenario <scenario_id> failed gates: <gate ids>\"\n+session_id: \"<run_id>\"\n+details:    {run_id, scenario_id, vendor, failed_gates:[{gate_id, detail}], skills_sha, repo_sha}\n+tags:\n+  - capability_gap                              # bare tag: what analyze_failures queries\n+  - capability_gap:scenario-parity/<scenario_id>/<first failed gate id>\n+  - failure_type:verification_failed\n+  - affected_skill:<skill_under_test>\n+  - severity:high\n+  - source:scenario-parity\n+  - vendor:<vendor>\n+  - scenario:<scenario_id>\n+```\n+\n+Notes:\n+- **Bare `capability_gap` tag**: `analyze_failures.query_memory` posts\n+  `tags: [\"capability_gap\"]` and the coordinator's recall matches tags by exact array\n+  overlap (`tags && p_tags`), so a prefixed tag alone would not be returned. Adding\n+  the bare tag is harmless to `_extract_tag` (it only reads `prefix:`-tags).\n+- **Stable `capability_gap` value** (`scenario-parity/<scenario>/<gate>`) so\n+  `/improve-harness` groups repeated nightly failures of the same gate into one\n+  finding whose frequency rises with repeated failures. `<gate>` is the first failed\n+  gate in **scenario declaration order** (not verdict order), so the key is stable.\n+- **Frequency unit is (run, vendor), not nights.** `/improve-harness` ranks raw\n+  memory entries (`rank_findings` counts entries per `capability_gap` value; its\n+  `deduplicate_findings` result is discarded — a known consumer bug owned by a\n+  separate change), and `POST /memory/query` does not return `session_id`. So two\n+  vendors failing the same gate in one run contribute frequency 2. This change does\n+  **not** repair the consumer's ranking; it documents the unit (runbook, memory\n+  conventions) and carries `run_id` inside `details` so a later consumer fix can\n+  collapse per run. The consumer test pins the actual behaviour: two vendors in one\n+  run → 2, plus a later run → 3.\n+- **Detail bound**: each `failed_gates[].detail` is truncated to 500 characters\n+  (also encoded as `maxLength: 500` in the contract), so a command gate's captured\n+  output cannot bloat memory or carry large log excerpts.\n+- **Only `fail` emits gaps.** `error` (CLI missing, timeout, fixture failure) and\n+  `skipped_budget` are infrastructure outcomes: recorded in the results store and the\n+  run summary, never as skill capability gaps. Judge findings never emit gaps (D3 of\n+  ri-15: judge is additive).\n+- **Severity `high`** for every deterministic failure (gates are explicit contract\n+  violations); not `critical`, which the D4 schema reserves for incidents.\n+- **Sinks** (`MemorySink` protocol): `CoordinatorMemorySink` — stdlib `urllib` POST to\n+  `${COORDINATION_API_URL}/memory/store` with `Authorization: Bearer ${COORDINATION_API_KEY}`\n+  (the coordinator's preferred header; `X-API-Key` is its legacy alias)\n+  (variable names configurable via `gaps.coordinator_url_env` / `gaps.api_key_env`;\n+  the defaults follow the repo-wide convention in\n+  `docs/coordination-detection-template.md`, whereas `analyze_failures.py` reads\n+  `COORDINATOR_URL` — the runbook requires both to name the same coordinator), a 10 s\n+  request timeout, and `agent_id` from config (default `agent-scenarios-nightly`).\n+  An unset URL variable means \"spool everything\" (no localhost fallback, so a\n+  misconfigured host never writes to an unintended coordinator). **Delivery is\n+  acknowledged only by HTTP 2xx with a JSON body whose `success` is `true`**; a 200\n+  with `success: false`, a non-JSON body, or any other status is a failed delivery\n+  and the entry is spooled (on emit) or kept (on flush). `SpoolMemorySink` —\n+  appends the identical payload to `<state>/gap-spool.jsonl`. The emitter tries the\n+  coordinator and spools any entry that fails. `agent-scenarios gaps flush` (also run\n+  at the start of every nightly) replays the spool and rewrites it with only the\n+  entries that still failed. No dependency on `skills/coordination-bridge` (the\n+  package must stay installable on its own).\n+- **Base-spec enum**: `openspec/specs/harness-engineering/spec.md` \"Capability Gap\n+  Detection\" still lists a closed four-value `source` enum, and the in-flight\n+  `add-a-judged-first-stage-to-coordinator-audit-triage` MODIFIES that requirement.\n+  The ADDED requirement here states that it extends that enum; whichever of the two\n+  changes archives second reconciles the enum text (adds `scenario-parity` to the\n+  MODIFIED copy, or files a follow-up MODIFIED delta) — tracked as task 6.4.\n+- **Shared tag schema**: `source:scenario-parity` is a *new vocabulary value*. It is\n+  documented in `docs/guides/memory-conventions.md` and added to the\n+  `SOURCE_VOCABULARY` constant in `skills/session-log/tests/test_memory_tag_conventions.py`\n+  (the doc's own rule for adding prefixes/values). `vendor:` and `scenario:` are\n+  auxiliary tags documented there too. The spec delta is an **ADDED** requirement in\n+  `harness-engineering` rather than a MODIFIED \"Capability Gap Detection\", because\n+  the in-flight `add-a-judged-first-stage-to-coordinator-audit-triage` already\n+  modifies that requirement and two MODIFIED deltas on one requirement collide at\n+  archive time.\n+- `/improve-harness` needs **no source-specific code** (it aggregates arbitrary\n+  `source:` values), but its memory query is **incompatible with the live API** and\n+  must be repaired in this change, or the emitted gaps are never read:\n+  `analyze_failures.query_memory` posts no `agent_id` (required by\n+  `MemoryQueryRequest`), sends no `X-API-Key`, sends `time_window_days` (not a request\n+  field — ignored), and reads `entries` while `/memory/query` returns a `memories`\n+  list envelope. The fix: send `agent_id` (default `improve-harness`, overridable),\n+  send `Authorization: Bearer` from `COORDINATION_API_KEY` when set, read `memories` (keeping\n+  `entries`/bare-list for older coordinators), and apply the time window client-side\n+  on `created_at`. A consumer test drives `query_memory` against a local\n+  `http.server` stub that enforces the real request model and returns the real\n+  envelope with the emitter's example payload, then feeds the result through\n+  `normalize_memory_entries` / `rank_findings` and asserts `scenario-parity` appears\n+  in the source set. The SKILL.md data-sources table gains a row.\n+\n+### D4 — Nightly runner with an explicit off-switch and caps\n+\n+`agent-scenarios nightly --config <path> [--dry-run]`. Config (validated by a pydantic\n+model; JSON schema in `contracts/nightly-config.schema.json`):\n+\n+```yaml\n+enabled: false                       # off by default — must be flipped by the operator\n+disable_file: ~/.config/agent-scenarios/DISABLED   # kill-file: presence disables\n+scenarios_dir: packages/agent-scenarios/scenarios\n+repo_root: ~/agentic-coding-tools    # checkout under test (repo_sha, skills_root base)\n+skills_root: skills                  # relative to repo_root\n+vendors: [claude, codex]             # allowlist ∩ scenario.vendors; must be ≥ 2\n+vendor_commands: {claude: \"claude -p {prompt} ...\", codex: \"codex exec {prompt} ...\"}\n+env_scrub: []        # extra names only; the built-in HERMETIC_SCRUB denylist always applies (D5)\n+env_set: {}          # extra overrides; may not name a denylisted variable (D5)\n+workspaces_root: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/workspaces\n+retain_failed_runs: 7\n+caps:                                # every key optional; these are the defaults\n+  max_pairs: 30\n+  max_pairs_per_vendor: 15\n+  max_wall_clock_minutes: 240\n+  per_pair_timeout_seconds: 1200\n+results: {path: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/results.jsonl}\n+findings: {path: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/findings/{run_id}.json}\n+gaps: {enabled: true, spool_path: ~/.local/state/agent-scenarios/gap-spool.jsonl, agent_id: agent-scenarios-nightly,\n+       coordinator_url_env: COORDINATION_API_URL, api_key_env: COORDINATION_API_KEY}\n+judge: {enabled: false}\n+```\n+\n+Ordered guards (each writes a `run` record with the matching status and exits 0\n+unless noted):\n+\n+0. Config file missing, unparsable or schema-invalid (including a vendor in\n+   `vendors` without a `vendor_commands` entry) → message on stderr, **exit 2, no\n+   record written** (the store path itself may be unknown).\n+1. `enabled: false` → `disabled`; **no executor constructed**.\n+2. `disable_file` exists → `disabled`.\n+3. Run lock (`flock` on `<state>/nightly.lock`) held → `locked`, exit 0 (overlap is\n+   expected-benign; systemd also prevents it).\n+4. Effective vendors = `config.vendors ∩ ⋃ scenario.vendors`. Fewer than 2 →\n+   `config_error` run record, exit 2, nothing launched.\n+5. Planned pairs = Σ over scenarios of |scenario.vendors ∩ config.vendors|. If\n+   `> max_pairs` or any vendor `> max_pairs_per_vendor` → `cap_exceeded`, **exit 2,\n+   nothing launched** (fail-closed rather than silently truncating coverage).\n+6. During the run, once elapsed ≥ `max_wall_clock_minutes`, remaining pairs are not\n+   launched and are recorded `skipped_budget`; run status `budget_exhausted`.\n+\n+Pair order is deterministic (scenarios sorted by id, then vendors in config order) so\n+a budget cut drops the same tail every night and trends stay comparable.\n+\n+**Spend cap rationale**: vendor CLIs do not expose dollar cost synchronously, so the\n+cap is expressed in launched pairs, wall clock and per-pair timeout — the levers the\n+runner controls. Dollar accounting belongs to the model-usage-ledger work.\n+\n+`--dry-run` runs guard 0, then evaluates guards 1–5 **without acting on them**: it\n+prints the off-switch state (`enabled`, kill-file present), the effective vendors,\n+the planned pair list and the cap evaluation, takes no lock, writes no record of any\n+kind, constructs no executor, and exits 0 (2 when guard 0, 4 or 5 would fail). It\n+deliberately ignores `enabled: false` because the runbook's pre-enable check\n+(task 7.2) runs it while the config is still disabled.\n+\n+Exit codes, highest precedence first: 2 config/cap error; 1 one or more scenario\n+`fail` (so systemd marks the unit failed and `OnFailure=` hooks can notify); 3 no\n+`fail` but the night is not green — one or more `error` results (infrastructure\n+broken: a CLI missing, keys expired, timeouts) **or** a `budget_exhausted` run (part\n+of the matrix was never tested); 0 only for a `completed` run whose pairs all passed,\n+and for `disabled` / `locked`. An incomplete matrix therefore never looks green.\n+\n+**Workspaces**: each pair runs in `<workspaces_root>/<run_id>/<scenario_id>--<vendor>/`\n+(default `workspaces_root` = `<state>/workspaces`). Workspaces (and their sibling\n+`.origin.git`) of `pass` and `skipped_budget` pairs are deleted after scoring;\n+`fail`/`error` workspaces are kept for diagnosis. At the start of each run, run\n+directories beyond the newest `retain_failed_runs` (default 7) are deleted, so disk\n+use is bounded at ~7 × 22 workspaces.\n+\n+**Spool concurrency**: emitting to and flushing the gap spool both take an exclusive\n+`flock` on `<spool>.lock`; `flush` rewrites the spool via a temp file + `os.replace`\n+under that lock, so a manual `gaps flush` concurrent with a nightly cannot drop or\n+duplicate entries.\n+\n+The runner calls the ri-15 `run_scenario` per scenario but passes a *filtered copy*\n+of the scenario (vendors ∩ allowlist) and checks the wall-clock budget between\n+pairs. To check budget between vendors of the same scenario it iterates scenarios ×\n+vendors itself and builds each `ParityMatrix` from single-vendor runs (the runner's\n+public API is unchanged).\n+\n+### D5 — Skill-under-test materialization and sandboxing in the executor\n+\n+A broken skill change can only fail the suite if the agent actually runs the changed\n+skill. `CLIVendorExecutor` gains:\n+\n+- `skills_root: Path | None` — when set, after fixture materialization it first\n+  checks that `skills_root/<skill_under_test>/SKILL.md` exists (else an executor\n+  `error` naming the skill, no vendor launched), then copies **the whole skills\n+  tree** — every top-level directory of `skills_root`, excluding `tests/`, `.venv/`,\n+  `__pycache__/` and `node_modules/` — into `workdir/.claude/skills/` and\n+  `workdir/.agents/skills/` (the project-local skill locations the vendor CLIs read).\n+  The whole tree is required, not just the skill under test: skills resolve helpers\n+  through sibling paths (`<skill-base-dir>/../worktree/scripts/worktree.py`,\n+  `../shared/checkout_policy.py`, `../session-log/scripts/…`), so a single-skill copy\n+  would make most live runs fail for reasons unrelated to the skill. This mirrors the\n+  runtime layout `install.sh` produces. Both directories are added to the fixture's\n+  `.git/info/exclude` so they never appear in agent commits or gate checks.\n+  `skills_sha` (git HEAD of the repo containing `skills_root`, `+dirty` if modified)\n+  is recorded on every result.\n+- **Hermetic environment (fail-closed, not configurable away)** — the executor owns\n+  a built-in `HERMETIC_SCRUB` denylist that config can extend (`env_scrub`) but never\n+  shrink: GitHub tokens (`GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`,\n+  `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`); every coordinator variable that\n+  `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/coordination_bridge.py` reads — the URL aliases\n+  `COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`, `AGENT_COORDINATOR_API_URL`, `AGENT_COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`,\n+  `AGENT_COORDINATOR_REST_PORT`, the API keys `COORDINATION_API_KEY`,\n+  `COORDINATOR_API_KEY`, and the Cloudflare Access service token\n+  `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` / `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET`; and `COORDINATOR_URL`, which\n+  `skills/improve-harness/scripts/analyze_failures.py` reads — plus the variables named\n+  by `gaps.api_key_env` and `gaps.coordinator_url_env`. After scrubbing and applying\n+  `env_set`, the executor **always** sets `COORDINATION_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9`\n+  (the discard port, which `_validate_url` accepts as loopback). The sentinel is\n+  needed because `coordination_bridge.py` falls back to `http://localhost:3000` when\n+  no URL variable is set — on the GX10 that *is* the live coordinator. `env_set` may\n+  not name any variable in the effective scrub set — the built-in denylist,\n+  `COORDINATION_API_URL`, any `env_scrub` entry, and the names in\n+  `gaps.api_key_env` / `gaps.coordinator_url_env` (the static part via schema\n+  `propertyNames`, the whole set by the pydantic model → guard 0, exit 2), so no\n+  valid config can re-open the live-coordinator path. Two drift tests guard the\n+  copies: `HERMETIC_SCRUB` ⊇ the bridge's `_HTTP_URL_ENV_KEYS`, `_API_KEY_ENV_KEYS` and\n+  CF variable names (skipped when the skills tree is absent), so a new bridge alias\n+  cannot silently bypass the scrub; and the config schema's\n+  `env_set.propertyNames` list equals `HERMETIC_SCRUB ∪ {COORDINATION_API_URL}`, so\n+  the schema and the executor cannot diverge. Vendor credentials (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, …) are\n+  untouched, and `HOME` is not replaced: vendor CLIs keep their auth there. MCP-based\n+  coordinator access and git transport credentials (SSH keys, credential helpers,\n+  `insteadOf` rewrites) configured under that HOME are therefore handled\n+  operationally — a dedicated nightly user/HOME with no coordinator MCP config and no\n+  GitHub push credentials (task 7.1) — and are named as a residual risk below.\n+- **`gh` shim** — the executor writes a stub `gh` executable into\n+  `<workdir>.bin/` (sibling, outside the workspace) and prepends it to the vendor's\n+  `PATH`, for every live run. It serves a deliberately small surface from a state file\n+  seeded by the fixture's optional `prs:` list: `gh auth status` (ok),\n+  `gh repo view --json`, `gh pr list|view|status --json`, `gh pr create` (records a\n+  PR whose head branch must exist on the local origin), `gh pr merge\n+  [--merge|--squash|--rebase] [--delete-branch]` (performs the merge with git against\n+  the local origin and marks the PR merged), and `gh api repos/{o}/{r}` returning\n+  `permissions.push: true` with branch protection reported absent (404). Any other\n+  invocation exits 1 and is appended to `<workdir>.bin/gh-unsupported.log`. This makes\n+  the merge-family skills runnable without GitHub, makes `pr` gates satisfiable\n+  against the local origin (the executor's post-run `gh pr view` resolves through the\n+  same shim), and guarantees no `gh` call reaches GitHub even if a credential leaks\n+  through `~/.config/gh`. **If the unsupported-call log is non-empty after the run,\n+  the verdict is forced to `error`** (\"gh shim: unsupported call …\"), so shim coverage\n+  gaps surface as infrastructure errors (exit 3, no capability gap) rather than being\n+  blamed on the skill; the shim's surface is widened by later changes as such errors\n+  appear.\n+- **Skill invocation** — copying the tree makes the skill *available*, not *used*.\n+  Every seed scenario's `task_prompt` therefore opens with an explicit invocation of\n+  its skill (`/<skill_under_test>` followed by the request), which both Claude Code\n+  and Codex resolve against the project-local skill directories; the guard test\n+  rejects a seed whose prompt does not contain `/<skill_under_test>`. Whether the\n+  agent then *follows* the skill is verified only indirectly, by gates that check the\n+  skill's distinctive artifacts (e.g. `## <Phase>` + `**Status**:` report sections,\n+  OpenSpec change layout); there is no vendor-neutral trace of skill loading. This is\n+  recorded as a residual risk and the live broken-skill drill (task 7.5) is the\n+  end-to-end check.\n+- `timeout_seconds` is fed from `caps.per_pair_timeout_seconds`, and a\n+  `TimeoutExpired` now yields an error message `vendor CLI timed out after <N>s`\n+  distinct from `vendor CLI unavailable` (today both return exit 127 with the same\n+  message, which would make the runbook's triage impossible).\n+\n+`FixtureSpec` gains `local_remote: bool = false`: create a bare repo at\n+`<workdir>.origin.git` (sibling, outside the workspace), `git remote add origin`, and\n+push the base branch; and `prs: list[{number, head, base, title}] = []`, the seed\n+state for the `gh` shim (head branches are pushed to the local origin at\n+materialization). Push/merge skills then operate against a local origin and never\n+reach GitHub. Gates for these scenarios use `command` checks such as\n+`git ls-remote origin <branch>` or `git -C ... merge-base --is-ancestor`.\n+\n+These are model/executor extensions with backward-compatible defaults; existing\n+scenarios and tests are unaffected.\n+\n+### D6 — Seed suite composition and self-test\n+\n+Skill families (constant `SKILL_FAMILIES` in `suite.py`; unknown skills map to\n+`other`, which does not count toward coverage):\n+\n+| Family | Skills |\n+|---|---|\n+| plan | `plan-feature`, `iterate-on-plan` |\n+| implement | `implement-feature`, `iterate-on-implementation` |\n+| validate | `validate-feature` |\n+| merge | `merge-pull-requests`, `cleanup-feature` |\n+\n+Suite (11 scenarios, all with `vendors: [claude, codex]` at minimum):\n+\n+| # | Scenario id | Skill | Discriminating gates (sketch) |\n+|---|---|---|---|\n+| 1 | `plan-feature-basic` (existing) | plan-feature | proposal/tasks exist on change branch; source untouched |\n+| 2 | `plan-feature-spec-delta` | plan-feature | `specs/<cap>/spec.md` has `## ADDED Requirements`, `#### Scenario:`; no `## Requirements` header |\n+| 3 | `iterate-on-plan-split-fused-task` | iterate-on-plan | fused \"X and Y\" task in fixture `tasks.md` is split; proposal untouched outside tasks; no source edit |\n+| 4 | `implement-feature-basic` (revised) | implement-feature | fix + test passes + commit on feature branch + branch pushed to local origin (replaces the GitHub `pr` gate) |\n+| 5 | `implement-feature-tdd-new-function` | implement-feature | new test file exists and passes; implementation exists; existing tests unmodified |\n+| 6 | `implement-feature-respects-scope` | implement-feature | change confined to `write_allow` from fixture `work-packages.yaml`; denied path untouched |\n+| 7 | `validate-feature-flags-failing-test` | validate-feature | validation report records a FAIL status; source NOT modified to make tests pass |\n+| 8 | `validate-feature-clean-pass` | validate-feature | report has machine-readable `## <Phase>` + `**Status**:` sections and a PASS verdict |\n+| 9 | `validate-feature-spec-gap` | validate-feature | report names the unimplemented spec scenario; no source edit |\n+| 10 | `merge-pull-requests-local-merge` | merge-pull-requests | feature commit is ancestor of `origin/main`; original main commit still ancestor (no force-push/rewrite) |\n+| 11 | `cleanup-feature-archive` | cleanup-feature | change dir moved under `openspec/changes/archive/`; feature branch deleted locally and on origin; main contains the merge |\n+\n+Each scenario has a **golden** and a **broken** `Outcome` in\n+`tests/scenario_outcomes/<scenario_id>.py`. The parametrized test asserts golden →\n+all gates pass and broken → at least one *named* gate fails. This proves every gate\n+set is satisfiable and discriminating without a vendor. Exact gate regexes and\n+fixture contents are authored during implementation and pinned by these tests.\n+\n+Guard test `test_seed_suite.py`: ≥ 10 scenarios; each of the four families has ≥ 2\n+scenarios; every scenario declares ≥ 2 vendors; every scenario has a golden/broken\n+outcome module; scenario ids are unique; every `task_prompt` contains\n+`/<skill_under_test>` (D5 skill invocation); no scenario uses a `pr` gate (GitHub side\n+effect) unless it also sets `local_remote` — enforced so live runs never need GitHub.\n+\n+### D7 — Deploy templates, never deployments\n+\n+`packages/agent-scenarios/deploy/`:\n+- `systemd/agent-scenarios-nightly.service.template` — `Type=oneshot`,\n+  `ExecStart=<uv> run --project <repo>/packages/agent-scenarios agent-scenarios nightly --config %h/.config/agent-scenarios/nightly.yaml`,\n+  `TimeoutStartSec` ≥ `max_wall_clock_minutes` + `per_pair_timeout_seconds` + 10 min\n+  (the budget is only checked between pairs, so the last pair may overrun it by up to\n+  one per-pair timeout; defaults → 270 min), `Nice=10`,\n+  `SuccessExitStatus=0` only (exit 1 and 3 mark the unit failed).\n+- `systemd/agent-scenarios-nightly.timer.template` — `OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:30`,\n+  `Persistent=false` (a missed night is skipped, not burst-replayed),\n+  `RandomizedDelaySec=15m`.\n+- `nightly.example.yaml` — `enabled: false`.\n+- A runbook `docs/guides/agent-scenarios-nightly.md`: install, dry-run, enable,\n+  disable (three ways: `systemctl --user disable --now`, kill-file, `enabled: false`),\n+  query examples, broken-skill drill.\n+\n+A test asserts the templates contain the placeholder tokens and that the example\n+config parses with `enabled: false`. Nothing in the change, its tests, or CI calls\n+`systemctl`.\n+\n+### D8 — CLI shape\n+\n+`__main__.py` becomes a subcommand dispatcher while keeping the current flags working:\n+`agent-scenarios validate --scenarios DIR` (and the legacy\n+`--scenarios DIR [--validate-only]` form, unchanged behaviour), `nightly`,\n+`results {query,trend,latest}`, `gaps flush`. The module docstring's stale\n+`--target`/`--out` flags (never implemented by ri-15) are removed. Subcommand modules own their own\n+`add_parser(subparsers)` so packages can be built in parallel without both editing\n+argument parsing in one file (only `wp-nightly` edits `__main__.py`).\n+\n+## Alternatives Considered\n+\n+| Alternative | Why rejected |\n+|---|---|\n+| Coordinator `scenario_results` table + API (Approach 2) | Migration/API/policy surface for a single-writer, low-volume dataset; loses data when coordinator is down unless spooled anyway. Kept as a future `ResultsStore` implementation. |\n+| GitHub Actions `schedule:` (Approach 3) | Requires vendor keys in CI secrets (trust-posture change); hosted runners lack vendor CLIs. |\n+| SQLite results file | Viable; rejected for JSONL's append-only/diffable simplicity at this volume. Revisit if records exceed ~1M or ad-hoc SQL is needed. |\n+| Emit gaps via session-log `### Capability Gaps Observed` | Session logs are per-change markdown in the repo; a nightly host job writing into `openspec/changes/**` would create commits/noise and break `openspec validate` (cf. PhaseRecord incident). |\n+| Emit gaps via `skills/coordination-bridge` `try_remember` | Would couple the standalone package to the skills tree layout; a 30-line stdlib client is simpler. |\n+| Truncate the matrix to fit the cap | Silently drops coverage and makes trends incomparable night to night; fail-closed is explicit. |\n+| Judge findings as capability gaps | Violates ri-15's \"judge is additive, never authoritative\"; they still go to the findings file. |\n+| Executor errors as capability gaps | Would blame skills for missing CLIs/keys/timeouts; recorded as `error` in the store instead. |\n+\n+## Assumptions (autonomous planning)\n+\n+This plan was produced non-interactively by the supervised autopilot PLAN phase.\n+Discovery questions were answered from the roadmap item, ri-15's artifacts and the\n+codebase:\n+\n+| # | Question | Assumed answer | Basis |\n+|---|---|---|---|\n+| A1 | Which skills count as \"plan / implement / validate / merge\"? | Families in D6; merge = `merge-pull-requests` + `cleanup-feature`. | Skill inventory; roadmap acceptance wording. |\n+| A2 | Which ≥ 2 vendors nightly? | `claude` + `codex` as the default allowlist (both already declared by the ri-15 seeds); others opt-in via config. | ri-15 seeds; vendor-status availability. |\n+| A3 | Trend store: file or coordinator table? | Append-only JSONL with query CLI (D2). | Gatekeeper preference for simplest durable store. |\n+| A4 | How do failures reach `/improve-harness`? | Memory API with new `source:scenario-parity` + spool fallback (D3). | improve-harness data sources; D4 tag schema doc rule for new values. |\n+| A5 | What is the \"spend cap\" unit? It deliberately stopped short of\n+the parts that make the harness *pay off* (its `tasks.md` §10 defers them here):\n+\n+- **Coverage** — only two seed scenarios exist (`plan-feature-basic`,\n+  `implement-feature-basic`); nothing exercises validate or merge skills.\n+- **Cadence** — `python -m agent_scenarios` is a lister/validator. There is no\n+  command that runs the suite end-to-end, no schedule, and no guard rails\n+  (off-switch, spend/size cap) that an unattended nightly run needs.\n+- **Feedback** — findings are written to a JSON file that nobody reads. The\n+  `/improve-harness` capability-gap pipeline never sees a scenario failure, so a skill\n+  regression caught by the harness does not become an improvement signal.\n+- **Trend** — a parity matrix is produced and discarded. There is no way to ask\n+  \"how has `validate-feature` been doing on `codex` over the last two weeks?\", which\n+  is the signal the roadmap wants to eventually gate dispatcher routing on.\n+- **Sensitivity to skill changes** — the live executor runs a vendor CLI in a bare\n+  fixture repo; nothing puts the *skill under test* (from the checkout being\n+  evaluated) into that workspace, so a broken skill change would not reliably show up\n+  in the suite at all.\n+\n+## What Changes\n+\n+1. **Seed suite (11 scenarios)** — 9 new scenarios plus the 2 existing ones, covering\n+   the four skill families: plan (3), implement (3), validate (3), merge (2). Every\n+   scenario declares at least 2 vendors. Each scenario ships with a scripted *golden*\n+   and *broken* `FakeExecutor` outcome so the test suite proves its gates are both\n+   satisfiable and discriminating. A suite-coverage guard test enforces the ≥10 /\n+   all-four-families / ≥2-vendors floor. `implement-feature-basic` is revised to gate\n+   on a push to a local bare `origin` instead of a real GitHub PR.\n+2. **Harness extensions for live runs** — fixture `local_remote` (a sibling bare repo\n+   wired as `origin`, so push/merge skills never touch GitHub) with seeded `prs:`; a\n+   small `gh` shim on every live run's `PATH` backed by that local origin, so the\n+   merge-family skills (which require `gh`) run without GitHub and unsupported `gh`\n+   calls surface as infrastructure errors; every seed prompt explicitly invokes its skill under test;\n+   a timeout reported distinctly from a missing CLI.\n+3. **Durable results store + query CLI** — an append-only, schema-versioned JSONL\n+   store (one record per run × scenario × vendor, plus a run-summary record) and\n+   `agent-scenarios results {query,trend,latest}` filtering by vendor, skill, skill\n+   family, scenario and time window.\n+4. **Capability-gap emission** — each deterministic scenario *failure* (not an\n+   executor/infra error) becomes an episodic-memory entry using the shared D4 tag\n+   schema with a new `source:scenario-parity` value, written through the coordinator\n+   `POST /memory/store` path with an offline JSONL spool fallback and a `gaps flush`\n+   replay command. `/improve-harness` needs no source-specific code, but its memory\n+   query is repaired to match the live `POST /memory/query` contract (`agent_id`, API\n+   key, `memories` envelope) — today it would never read the emitted gaps; self-hosted GX10 runners (the roadmap's CI-migration item) are not in place yet.\n+- **Effort**: M\n+\n+### Selected Approach\n+\n+**Approach 1** (autonomous planning, recorded in `design.md` → \"Assumptions\n+(autonomous planning)\"). coverage floor\n+\n+The agent-scenarios package SHALL ship a seed suite of at least 10 scenarios covering the plan, implement, validate and merge skill families, with at least 2 scenarios per family and at least 2 declared vendors per scenario, every scenario's task prompt SHALL explicitly invoke its skill under test, and a guard test SHALL fail the build when the suite drops below this floor.\n+\n+#### Scenario: the shipped suite meets the coverage floor\n+- **WHEN** the guard test loads every `*.scenario.yaml` under `packages/agent-scenarios/scenarios/`\n+- **THEN** it SHALL find at least 10 scenarios with unique ids\n+- **AND** each of the families plan, implement, validate and merge SHALL be represented by at least 2 scenarios according to the package's skill-family map\n+- **AND** every scenario SHALL declare at least 2 vendors\n+- **AND** every scenario's `task_prompt` SHALL contain `/<skill_under_test>`\n+\n+#### Scenario: a seed prompt that does not invoke its skill fails the guard\n+- **WHEN** the guard test finds a seed scenario whose `task_prompt` does not contain `/<skill_under_test>`\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail and name the scenario id\n+\n+#### Scenario: removing scenarios below the floor fails the guard\n+- **WHEN** the guard test runs against a suite directory containing only 9 scenarios, or with no merge-family scenario\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail and name the unmet floor\n+\n+### Requirement: Seed scenarios are self-tested as satisfiable and discriminating\n+\n+Every seed scenario SHALL have a scripted golden outcome and a scripted broken outcome for the fake executor, and the test suite MUST show that the golden outcome passes all goal gates while the broken outcome fails at least one named gate.\n+\n+#### Scenario: golden outcome passes every gate\n+- **WHEN** a seed scenario is run through the runner with the fake executor scripted with its golden outcome\n+- **THEN** every vendor result SHALL have deterministic status `pass`\n+\n+#### Scenario: broken outcome fails a named gate\n+- **WHEN** the same scenario is run with its broken outcome\n+- **THEN** every vendor result SHALL have deterministic status `fail`\n+- **AND** the failed gate ids SHALL include the gate id named by the broken outcome\n+\n+#### Scenario: a seed scenario without outcomes is rejected\n+- **WHEN** a scenario file is added without a corresponding golden/broken outcome module\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail and name the scenario id\n+\n+### Requirement: Live runs never reach real GitHub\n+\n+Seed scenarios SHALL NOT depend on GitHub side effects. Push and merge behaviour MUST be exercised against a fixture-local bare `origin` repository, every live run SHALL resolve `gh` to a local shim instead of the real GitHub CLI, and the live executor SHALL always remove a built-in denylist of GitHub and coordinator credential and address variables from the vendor subprocess environment and point skill coordinator detection at an unreachable address; configuration MAY extend the denylist but MUST NOT remove from it or override the unreachable address.\n+\n+#### Scenario: local remote fixture\n+- **WHEN** a scenario fixture sets `local_remote: true`\n+- **THEN** fixture materialization SHALL create a bare repository outside the workspace, register it as `origin`, and push the base branch to it\n+\n+#### Scenario: PR gates require a local remote\n+- **WHEN** the guard test finds a seed scenario with a `pr` goal gate and `local_remote` not set\n+- **THEN** the guard test SHALL fail\n+\n+#### Scenario: credential variables are scrubbed\n+- **WHEN** the live executor runs a vendor command with an empty `env_scrub` while `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `COORDINATOR_API_KEY`, `COORDINATOR_HTTP_URL`, `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` and `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` are set in the runner's environment\n+- **THEN** none of those variables SHALL be present in the vendor subprocess environment\n+\n+#### Scenario: config cannot re-open the live coordinator path\n+- **WHEN** a nightly config sets `env_set` with a key `COORDINATION_API_URL`, `COORDINATOR_URL`, any other built-in denylisted variable, any config, `COORDINATION_API_URL` in the vendor subprocess environment SHALL equal `http://127.0.0.1:9`\n+\n+#### Scenario: the denylist covers every coordinator variable the skills read\n+- **WHEN** the unavailable CLI\n+\n+### Requirement: Durable per-vendor per-skill results store\n+\n+Each nightly run SHALL append one schema-versioned result record per scenario and vendor, and one run-summary window\n+- **WHEN** an operator runs `agent-scenarios results query --vendor codex --skill validate-feature --since <date>`\n+- **THEN** only `result` records matching that vendor, skill and window status `fail` for scenario `validate-feature-clean-pass` on vendor `codex` with failed gate `report-has-status`\n+- **THEN** the emitter SHALL send one entry whose `capability_gap:` tag names the first failed gate in scenario declaration order, with tags including `capability_gap`, `capability_gap:scenario-parity/validate-feature-clean-pass/report-has-status`, `failure_type:verification_failed`, `affected_skill:validate-feature`, `severity:high`, `source:scenario-parity` and `vendor:codex`\n+- **AND** the entry's `session_id` SHALL be the nightly `run_id`\n+\n+#### Scenario: errors and judge findings do not emit gaps\n+- **WHEN** a result has deterministic status `error` or `skipped_budget`, or passes gates but carries LLM-judge findings\n+- **THEN** no capability-gap entry SHALL be emitted for it\n+\n+#### Scenario: coordinator unreachable spools entries\n+- **WHEN** the coordinator memory endpoint is unreachable during emission\n+- **THEN** every entry SHALL be appended to the gap spool file and none SHALL be lost\n+\n+#### Scenario: spool replay\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios gaps flush` runs and the coordinator is reachable\n+- **THEN** spooled entries SHALL be delivered and removed from the spool\n+- **AND** entries that still fail delivery SHALL remain in the spool\n+\n+#### Scenario: an application-level rejection is not a delivery\n+- **WHEN** the coordinator memory endpoint answers HTTP 200 with `success: false`, a non-JSON body, or a non-2xx status\n+- **THEN** the entry SHALL be treated as undelivered: spooled on emission and kept in the spool on flush\n+\n+#### Scenario: no coordinator URL configured spools instead of guessing\n+- **WHEN** the variable named by `gaps.coordinator_url_env` is unset\n+- **THEN** every entry SHALL be spooled and no HTTP request SHALL be made to any host\n+\n+#### Scenario: concurrent flush and emission lose nothing\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios gaps flush` and a nightly emission touch the spool concurrently\n+- **THEN** after both finish, every entry SHALL be either delivered or present exactly once in the spool\n+\n+#### Scenario: a deliberately broken skill change produces a capability gap\n+- **WHEN** the suite runs against a skills root in which a skill under test has been deliberately broken so that its scenario's gates fail\n+- **THEN** the run SHALL record a `fail` result for that scenario\n+- **AND** a capability-gap entry with `affected_skill` equal to that skill and `source:scenario-parity` SHALL be emitted\n+- **AND** `/improve-harness` failure analysis over that entry SHALL rank a finding for that capability gap with `scenario-parity` in its source set\n+\n+### Requirement: Nightly runner with off-switch and spend caps\n+\n+The package SHALL provide a nightly command that runs the suite across an allowlist of at least 2 vendors under explicit size and time caps, and that does nothing unless explicitly enabled.\n+\n+#### Scenario: disabled by default\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios nightly` runs with a config whose `enabled` is false\n+- **THEN** no executor SHALL be constructed and no vendor command SHALL run\n+- **AND** a `run` record with status `disabled` SHALL be appended and the command SHALL exit 0\n+\n+#### Scenario: kill-file disables an enabled config\n+- **WHEN** the config is enabled and the configured `disable_file` exists\n+- **THEN** the run SHALL behave as disabled\n+\n+#### Scenario: over-cap plan refuses to start\n+- **WHEN** the planned scenario×vendor pairs exceed `caps.max_pairs`, or any vendor's pairs exceed `caps.max_pairs_per_vendor`\n+- **THEN** no pair SHALL be launched\n+- **AND** a `run` record with status `cap_exceeded` SHALL be appended and the command SHALL exit 2\n+\n+#### Scenario: wall-clock budget stops launching new pairs\n+- **WHEN** elapsed run time reaches `caps.max_wall_clock_minutes` with pairs remaining\n+- **THEN** remaining pairs SHALL NOT be launched and SHALL be recorded with status `skipped_budget`\n+- **AND** the `run` record status SHALL be `budget_exhausted`\n+- **AND** when no executed pair has status `fail`, the command SHALL exit 3, never 0\n+\n+#### Scenario: fewer than two effective vendors is a config error\n+- **WHEN** the vendor allowlist intersected with the suite's declared vendors yields fewer than 2 vendors\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 2 without launching any pair\n+- **AND** a `run` record with status `config_error` SHALL be appended\n+\n+#### Scenario: invalid config writes nothing\n+- **WHEN** the config file is unparsable, violates the config schema, or lists a vendor without a `vendor_commands` entry\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 2 with a message naming the problem, launch no pair and write no record\n+\n+#### Scenario: overlapping runs are refused\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run starts while another holds the run lock\n+- **THEN** it SHALL record status `locked` and exit 0 without launching any pair\n+\n+#### Scenario: dry run plans without executing\n+- **WHEN** `agent-scenarios nightly --dry-run` runs with a valid config, whether `enabled` is true or false\n+- **THEN** it SHALL print the off-switch state, the effective vendors, the planned pairs and the cap evaluation\n+- **AND** it SHALL NOT construct an executor, take the run lock, launch any pair or write any record\n+\n+#### Scenario: failing scenarios make the run exit non-zero\n+- **WHEN** a completed nightly run has at least one `fail` result\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 1 after writing results, findings and gaps, whether or not the wall-clock budget was exhausted\n+\n+#### Scenario: an infrastructure-only failure is not a green night\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run has no `fail` result but at least one `error` result or the run status `budget_exhausted`\n+- **THEN** the command SHALL exit 3\n+- **AND** no capability-gap entry SHALL be emitted for the `error` results\n+\n+#### Scenario: workspaces are bounded\n+- **WHEN** a nightly run finishes\n+- **THEN** the workspaces of its `pass` pairs SHALL have been deleted and those of its `fail` and `error` pairs SHALL remain\n+- **AND** at the start of the next run, run directories older than the newest `retain_failed_runs` SHALL be deleted\n+\n+### Requirement: Schedule shipped as templates only\n+\n+The change SHALL ship the nightly schedule Memory Tag Conventions\n\nEpisodic memory tags are arbitrary strings, but capability-gap signals use a shared prefix schema so multiple emitters and consumers interoperate. This document defines the tag schema, source vocabulary, and usage patterns.\n\n## Tag Schema\n\nAll capability-gap entries use the `prefix:value` format:\n\n| Prefix | Values | Description |\n|--------|--------|-------------|\n| `failure_type` | `scope_violation`, `verification_failed`, `lock_unavailable`, `timeout`, `convergence_failed`, `context_exhaustion` | Categorizes the failure mode |\n| `capability_gap` | Free text | Describes what capability was missing from the harness |\n| `affected_skill` | Skill name (kebab-case) | Which skill was impacted |\n| `severity` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | Impact severity |\n| `source` | `self-reported`, `coordinator-emitted`, `session-log`, `transcript-mined`, `scenario-parity` | Which emitter produced this signal |\n| `vendor` | Vendor id (`claude`, `codex`, ...) | Auxiliary; which vendor CLI failed a scenario (`scenario-parity` entries) |\n| `scenario` | Scenario id (kebab-case) | Auxiliary; which agent-scenarios scenario failed (`scenario-parity` entries) |\n\n### Example Tags\n\n```\nfailure_type:scope_violation\ncapability_gap:agent could not detect circular dependency in DAG\naffected_skill:implement-feature\nseverity:high\nsource:self-reported\n```\n\n## Source Vocabulary\n\nFive sources emit capability-gap signals into the shared tag schema:\n\n| Source | Emitter | When |\n|--------|---------|------|\n| `self-reported` | Agent via `remember` MCP tool | Agent encounters a task failure and self-reports |\n| `coordinator-emitted` | Coordinator audit-triage background task | LLM classifier detects struggle patterns in audit batches |\n| `session-log` | Session-log skill at phase boundaries | Agent fills `### Capability Gaps Observed` section in session-log |\n| `transcript-mined` | `/collect-transcripts` deep-analysis pass | LLM analysis flags struggle patterns in raw transcripts |\n| `scenario-parity` | `agent-scenarios nightly` gap emitter | A seed scenario's deterministic goal gate failed for a vendor |\n\nEach source has a known bias profile:\n- **self-reported** under-reports struggle (agents don't stop to introspect when struggling)\n- **coordinator-emitted** misses tool-loop friction (only sees MCP/HTTP boundary)\n- **session-log** catches what the agent noticed but may miss timing details\n- **transcript-mined** catches everything but is the most expensive to run\n\n- **scenario-parity** is deterministic (goal gates, not a judge) but samples only the seed scenarios; executor errors and budget skips are never emitted\n\n### Scenario-parity entries\n\n`agent-scenarios nightly` emits one entry per failing (scenario, vendor) pair via `POST /memory/store`, tagged `capability_gap` (bare, so the `recall` tag filter matches), `capability_gap:scenario-parity/<scenario_id>/<first failed gate>`, `failure_type:verification_failed`, `affected_skill:<skill>`, `severity:high`, `source:scenario-parity`, `vendor:<vendor>` and `scenario:<scenario_id>`. The `capability_gap` value is stable per gate, so repeated nightly failures group into one `/improve-harness` finding.\n\n**Frequency unit**: `/improve-harness` ranks raw memory entries, so a finding's frequency counts failing (run, vendor) pairs, not nights. Two vendors failing the same gate in one run contribute 2. `details.run_id` carries the nightly run id so a later consumer fix can collapse per run (`POST /memory/query` does not return `session_id`).\n\nCross-source agreement (same gap surfaced by 2+ sources) is the strongest signal.\n\n## Deduplication\n\n`/improve-harness` deduplicates findings on the tuple `(capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id)`. When the same gap appears from multiple sources, all sources are preserved in a multi-source list. This cross-referencing is itself valuable signal.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Recording a capability gap (agent self-report)\n\nUse the `remember` MCP tool with the shared tag schema:\n\n```\nremember(\n    event_type=\"discovery\",\n    summary=\"Agent could not detect circular dependency\",\n    tags=[\n        \"failure_type:scope_violation\",\n        \"capability_gap:missing circular dependency detection\",\n        \"affected_skill:implement-feature\",\n        \"severity:high\",\n        \"source:self-reported\",\n    ],\n)\n```\n\n### Querying capability gaps\n\nUse `recall` with tag filters:\n\n```\nrecall(tags=[\"failure_type:scope_violation\"], limit=20)\nrecall(tags=[\"source:session-log\"], limit=50)\nrecall(tags=[\"severity:critical\"], limit=10)\n```\n\n### Adding new tag prefixes\n\nNew prefixes can be added without code changes -- the memory API accepts arbitrary strings. Document new prefixes in this file and update the test constants in `skills/session-log/tests/test_memory_tag_conventions.py`.\n\n## Memory Layers (episodic only)\n\nThe coordinator exposes a single persistent memory layer: **episodic memory**\n(`memory_episodic`). It is the only layer with both a writer and a reader — the\n`remember`/`recall` MCP tools, the `POST /memory/store` and `POST /memory/query`\nHTTP endpoints, the bridge `try_remember`/`try_recall` helpers, and the\ncapability-gap tag pipeline documented above all operate on it.\n\n### Decision (ri-15): working and procedural memory were descoped\n\nMigration `004_memory_tables.sql` originally declared three layers — episodic,\n`memory_working`, and `memory_procedural` — but only episodic was ever wired.\n`memory_working` and `memory_procedural` had no code path storing to or querying\nfrom them; they were empty tables with documented ambitions and no consumer.\n\nRoadmap item **ri-15** resolved this \"third state\" by **removing the two\nunconsumed layers** (Option B) rather than wiring them (Option A). Option A was\nrejected on effort and fit: it would have required new SQL functions, new\ncoordinator HTTP endpoints (`coordination_api.py` + `http_proxy.py`), new\n`MemoryService` methods, new bridge helpers, and a live-coordinator-backed test —\na cross-service change well beyond the item's budget — and the procedural schema\n(`skill_name`-keyed, `steps`/`success_count`/`failure_count`) is a poor fit for\nper-item roadmap learnings.\n\nRoadmap learnings keep their existing, working home: `learnings/<item-id>.md`\nfiles, written by `skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/learning.py` and read back by\n`skills/autopilot-roadmap/scripts/replanner.py`. That file-based loop already has\na writer and a reader, so no coordinator memory layer is needed for it.\n\nRemoval migration: `agent-coordinator/database/migrations/031_drop_unused_memory_tables.sql`.\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1791760674653},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"The memory conventions doc looks good - it documents the new `scenario-parity` source.
